close_reason: Superseded by bd:JMAP-1j9k.9 (closed by commit b6d2ebb on 2026-05-17). The workspace adopted the OPPOSITE policy: public method-input Params structs do NOT use #[non_exhaustive]; forward-compat for future spec-defined fields is the flatten-ed 'extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>' field per workspace AGENTS.md extras-preservation policy. Adding #[non_exhaustive] to EmailGetParams/EmailCopyParams/MailboxSetParams/EmailSubmissionSetParams/EmailImportInput/EmailParseParams would now be the regression — those six structs and the rest of the sibling Params structs across calendars/contacts/filenode/metadata/tasks already follow the no-non_exhaustive + extras-flatten canonical shape established by EmailGetParams. The bead's own agent-authored recommendation was correct at the time it was filed (2026-05-15) but the workspace decision rolled the other way two days later. The 6 mail-client structs the bead lists already carry the workspace-canonical 'extra' flatten field for vendor forward-compat; that's the intended design.
description:
Six public input-parameter structs in src/methods/mod.rs lack #[non_exhaustive]:

  - EmailGetParams (line 42)
  - EmailCopyParams (line 69)
  - MailboxSetParams (line 89)
  - EmailSubmissionSetParams (line 113)
  - EmailImportInput<'a> (line 149)
  - EmailParseParams (line 255)

The three Deserialize response structs (EmailImportCreated, EmailImportResponse, EmailParseResponse) DO have it. SessionClient does too. So this is an inconsistent pattern, not a blanket oversight.

Risk: every one of these structs corresponds to RFC 8621 method arguments that may grow. RFC 8621 §4.1.8 lists fetchTextBodyValues, fetchHTMLBodyValues, fetchAllBodyValues, maxBodyValueBytes, bodyProperties — but the spec authors could add more in a future revision (RFC errata, new draft features, see e.g. draft-ietf-jmap-quotas which extends method args). Without #[non_exhaustive], any new typed field is a breaking change for callers who used struct-literal construction.

Mitigation already in place:
  - EmailGetParams, MailboxSetParams, EmailSubmissionSetParams, EmailParseParams derive Default — callers using `..Default::default()` are protected against ADDITIONS of typed fields. But struct literals with all fields named WILL break, and the Rust compiler error message is unhelpful.
  - EmailCopyParams (required from_account_id) and EmailImportInput (required blob_id / mailbox_ids / borrowed lifetimes) do NOT derive Default. Callers MUST use struct literal — which means ANY new typed field is breaking with no mitigation.

The `extra: serde_json::Map<...>` flatten field handles VENDOR-extension growth via the workspace extras policy. But it does NOT handle SPEC-defined typed-field growth — the value lives in `extra` until someone promotes it to a typed field, and that promotion is the breaking change.

Action: add #[non_exhaustive] to all six. Cookie-cutter implication (workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates"): same sweep across the six sibling extension-client crates' Set/Get/Copy/Import/Parse params types.

Mark says NO HUMAN — I have a clear recommendation:
Recommendation: add #[non_exhaustive] to all six, accept the modest caller-side breakage today (callers must add `..Default::default()` or use a constructor) in exchange for safe future spec-field additions.
title: Missing #[non_exhaustive] on public input param structs: EmailGetParams, EmailCopyParams, MailboxSetParams, EmailSubmissionSetParams, EmailImportInput, EmailParseParams
